answers.reason: Abila Lysaniou is the settlement identified with Souq Wadi Barada. No candidate is supplied.
Adasa, the battle site in 1 Maccabees 7:40, is identified here with Khirbet Adasa. Hadashah in Joshua 15:37 is a different settlement in the Judah lowlands.
Adulis is the ancient Red Sea port in present-day Eritrea. None of the candidates denotes that settlement.
The supplied location places Ama along the Uqnu in Mesopotamia. Amad and Amam are settlements in Israel, while Amaw is explicitly a region between Aleppo and Carchemish.
Amate is located along the Uqnu, unlike Hamath at Hama or Hammath at Tiberias. No candidate has the same geographic identification.
Arbela is explicitly identified with Horbat Arbel in Galilee. The candidate Beth-arbel is identified with Tall Irbid, a different site.
This Arsinoe is an Egyptian settlement in the region between Maghfar and Lake Timsah. Syene is Aswan, and none of the other candidates denotes the supplied location.
Batanea is a historical region associated with Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee. Ecbatana is a city in Media, and no Bashan candidate is supplied.
The supplied identification makes Belamon another name for Abel-beth-maacah. That referent is absent from the candidates; Baal-hamon and the Baal-meon aliases are different places.
Carthage is the ancient North African city near modern Tunis. None of the candidates denotes that city.
